b: People are energized when they feel their power to make a difference.
Passivity is our natural response to lack of control. If you can’t control it, why try?
We don’t learn helplessness. We learn we have power. Experiencing control teaches us our actions matter.
The cure for passivity is results, not a pep talk.
Habitually solving people’s problems reinforces helplessness.
Ask: “What’s one thing you could try?”
People disengage when you make decisions for them. Making choices feels powerful.
Ask: “How would you like to approach this?”
Give people achievable challenges that require effort.
Ask: “What’s one result you could influence today?”
Show them how their actions change outcomes.
Ask: “What changed because of your contribution?”
People who follow orders aren’t necessarily engaged.
Give room to think, decide, and take ownership.
Ask: “What would you do if this decision were yours?”
Create conditions where people discover their control.
Stop asking, “How can I get people motivated?”
Start asking, “What am I doing that makes people feel powerless?”
People need a chance to make a difference.
Where are you unintentionally replacing someone’s initiative with your own?
